card.name: British spellings and place-name endings
card.fires_on: Word endings inside British-style words, such as -ising, -isable, -ised and -oured, and endings of UK place names like Lothians, Oxfordshire. It also fires on a few odd spots like 'ON' and 'etc'.

modes.label: British -ise/-our endings
modes.description: The ending piece of a word spelled the British way, such as -ising, -isable, -ised, -oured.
modes.example: white coated horses are much less troubled by horseflies than their dark-col<<oured>> relatives

modes.label: UK place names
modes.description: The ending of a place name in Britain or a regional abbreviation.
modes.example: I also cover Edinburgh and the Loth<<ians>> Renewable Energy - The Future

modes.label: Odd stray spots
modes.description: Scattered short pieces inside names or titles, such as 'etc' or 'it' in an odd spot.
modes.example: Under the Health & Safety<< etc>>. Act 1974 employers

card.writes: It seems to favor British-spelling endings (-ised, -ise forms) over other continuations, though the output tokens are mixed.
card.plain: It lights up on the ends of British-spelled words and UK place names.
